text:
nina: PSA from today's sponsor dinner 1 64b3fb37d3fb — the plated "chef's choice" had dairy hidden in the sauce. if you have allergies, double-check before you eat.
omar: Ugh, sorry that happened. Did they have a separate veg/vegan option on the menu?
nina: There was a label but it was vague. I asked and they offered a plain grain bowl from the back kitchen. Took 20min.
pat: Conference dining tip: carry a small card that says your diet/allergies in local language. Saved me in Tokyo when ingredients were confusing.
ash: Also: portable silicone travel bowl + spork = you can get a takeaway salad and eat in the lounge instead of waiting for the seated dinner.
rafa: If anyone needs emergency snacks, there's a 24h grocery 2 blocks from the venue. I ran over and grabbed hummus + pita.
travel-bot: FYI: If you buy food due to dietary restrictions, you can submit as an out-of-pocket travel meal on the expense form. Attach receipt and note reason.
omar: Quick micro-hack for leftovers: request a small sealed container from staff, then put in the hotel mini-fridge. prevents spoilage if you have to travel next day.
nina: Thank you all. Saved the team: I grabbed pita and split with @pat. Also filed expense.
pat: tiny checklist I use when traveling to events:```
- allergy card in phone + paper
- 1x snack bar
- reusable utensil set
- Metro map + grocery nearby saved in maps
```
ash: Reusable utensil rec: light titanium spork from REI. folds tiny.
rafa: Also shoutout to venue staff who were helpful once we explained. Major kudos. :clap:
pat: Poll: do you want me to add a "diet & emergency food" section to the offsite logistics doc? react with :thumbsup: or :thumbsdown:
nina: :thumbsup: yes please
omar: :thumbsup:
travel-bot: Reminder: Add receipts and short notes for any meals submitted under special-diet expenses. Submit within 7 days.
